must_preserve: P07 relation/authority kind and decision semantics
12 F7 states / prior 19 source authority kinds

options.name: bounded pure Python hardening and narrowed claim
options.security_property: resist named data/transplant attacks up to explicitly agreed boundary with trusted Python code/callsite
options.attacker_still_can: arbitrary coordinated mutation of trusted Python computation and output; present coordinated witness forges
options.interface: minimal; strengthened owner checks and tests, explicit limited threat contract
options.provenance: existing interpreter; new hostile court/independent rerun
options.architecture_warrant: HQ threat/claim authority decision if accepted nonforgeability ceiling changes
options.F7_effect: potential quick limited qualification only; not full commissioned claim

options.name: opaque native C custody-only capability
options.security_property: uninspectable/unreplaceable native owner ledger under Python-reflection-only attacker
options.attacker_still_can: replace Python entrypoints and F7 receipt processing; native process memory under stronger native attacker
options.interface: native owner handle and native exact decision; Python adapter remains vulnerable unless reliance moves
options.provenance: native binary hashes plus Python ABI and tests
options.F7_effect: P07 custody hardening, NOT end-to-end full nonforgeability

options.name: native atomic owner decision and trusted consumption
options.security_property: end-to-end decision integrity under Python reflection only IF no trusted Python-callable seam can override result and consumer relies on native verifier
options.attacker_still_can: rewrite Python-visible UI/outputs outside trusted consumer; native compromise if permitted
options.interface: P07+F7 decision/verification trust boundary expanded, opaque authenticated receipt
options.provenance: new native ABI/test/custody replay and independent hostile system court
options.F7_effect: can close stronger model only with proven consumer trust boundary

options.name: isolated trusted service / IPC
options.security_property: P07/F7 custody and decision insulated from untrusted Python in separate process; authenticity only at trusted verifier
options.attacker_still_can: fake client-side Python return or bypass Python verifier; OS peer compromise if unprotected
options.interface: serialized exact request/receipt, IPC authentication, replay binding, external trusted consumer
options.provenance: server binary, protocol, identity, environment, transport replay and end-to-end court
options.F7_effect: strongest feasible trust partition for arbitrary Python client, not automatic without trusted consumption

options.name: trusted interpreter/code TCB restriction
options.security_property: protect ordinary adversarial inputs by excluding attacker ability to run or mutate trusted Python code
options.attacker_still_can: caller data manipulation tested by owner checks; arbitrary code disallowed by assumption
options.interface: unchanged or bounded Python owner; deployment controls/explicit threat statement
options.F7_effect: conserves contract semantically, cannot claim resistance to hostile code execution

decision_tree: HQ first fixes exact adversary powers and trusted computing base (named reflection vs arbitrary Python code vs native/OS compromise).
If arbitrary Python can mutate final F7 consumer/output, custody-only C is NOT sufficient; commission end-to-end trust boundary (N2 or I1) under architecture warrant.
If trusted Python callsite/consumer are excluded from attacker power, choose minimal P1/N1 after proving coordinated attack refusal and five positives, or explicitly narrow claim with an HQ decision.
Do not adopt any remedy until independent adversarial and productive courts, runtime qualification, and HQ explicit adoption.
